text:
mira: Quick question — for the v2->v3 streaming migration, are we comfortable running two shims simultaneously (envelope shim + frame shim) behind a new 'cohabitation operator', or should we prefer a single sidecar per node? Thinking about tenant isolation, rollout flexibility, and operational cost. cc @jason @kate :thinking:
jason: I lean operator. Sidecars are simple but they balloon memory/ops when tenants are mixed. Operator gives us centralized policy control per-tenant.
kate: Operator + tenant feature-flag sounds right. Need very clear rollback paths and health gates. Also watch out for double prefix-caching.
samir: Tradeoff summary: operator = infra work (CRD + controller) but cheaper at scale; sidecar = simpler codepath but expensive to run and upgrade.
mira: I sketched a small proposal: operator takes a match rule (header or tenant tag) -> route to {legacy-shim, frame-shim, passthrough}. Hookpoints for shim latency/error metrics and tracing. Thoughts?
jason: Paste the rule format please. We should reuse our existing routing CRD rather than inventing a new one.
mira: ```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: ShimRoute
spec:
  match:
    tenantRegex: "^.*-migrating$"
    header: "x-client-version"
  route:
    primary: newFramer
    fallback: legacyEnvelope
  metrics:
    - shim_latency_ms
    - shim_errors_total
  billingTag: "framer-v3"
```
kate: Good. Reuse the CRD. Add `maxInflight` and `batchingEnabled` flags so operator can tune perf per-tenant.
mira: Agreed. Also want a circuit-breaker: if shim error-rate > 5% over 5m, auto-switch tenant to passthrough and alert. Expose diagnostic endpoint for tenants to see routing reason.
infra-bot: heads-up: any operator that modifies routing needs infra-security review and a runbook. Please file in #eng-infra.
samir: Telemetry note: we MUST emit shim-level spans + a `shim_path` baggage key tying request_id -> shim. Otherwise tracing across operator/shim/runtime is painful.
jason: +1. Rollout plan: canary 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated gates on p95 latency and error-rate, and manual checkpoints.
kate: Client-compat: some old clients send chunked frames without headers. Operator should detect by handshake and route to frame-shim even if header missing.
mira: Plan: header check first, then payload-sniﬃng of initial frame for `v3-init` token, then fallback. We'll document detection heuristics.
jason: Billing: new framer is cheaper per-token. Ensure billing logs include `shim_type` so customers and finance can reconcile costs.
mira: I'll add `billingTag` to CRD (see snippet). I'll open an RFC follow-up PR with operator design + runbook. Targeting a small canary next week.
kate: Add a smoke test for prefix-cache correctness — last migration tripped our cache and p95 spiked.
samir: Ops asks for a tenant opt-in script/console toggle that flips the tenant tag; prefer UI toggle + API for audit.
mira: I'll wire a console toggle that writes tenant metadata; operator will watch that. Also adding an endpoint `/debug/routing?tenant=...` to explain why a tenant is on legacy.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: branch `operator/cohabitation-probe` created and pushed. CI: running.
jason: Nice, ping me when RFC PR is ready; I’ll review operator schema and rollout gates.
kate: If nobody objects, +1 for operator-first approach. :rocket:
